title: Sequential Logic Circuits - Latches, Flip-Flops, Counters, FSM
subtitle: Latches, flip-flops, counters, timing waveforms, Mealy and Moore diagrams and tables - design for functionality and timing
subtopics: Timing waveforms (design from waveform with D flip-flops)
Mealy and Moore State Diagrams (incl. non-overlapping 1011 Moore FSM)
Synchronous design for functionality and timing

readingSections.title: 1. Why Sequential? SR and D Latches (From Zero)
readingSections.quickSummary: Combinational forgets. Sequential remembers via feedback. A latch is the smallest memory: one bit held in a loop.
content: Combinational output depends only on present inputs. Sequential output depends on present inputs AND stored past - it has memory elements plus combinational next-state logic, all stepped by a clock. Counters, registers and FSMs are sequential.

The SR latch (NOR version): two cross-coupled NOR gates. $S=1,R=0$ sets $Q=1$. $S=0,R=1$ resets $Q=0$. $S=0,R=0$ holds (memory). $S=1,R=1$ is forbidden (both outputs forced $0$, and releasing together races). $Q$ and $\bar{Q}$ are complements in valid states.

The NAND SR latch flips polarity: $S=0,R=0$ forbidden, $S=1,R=1$ holds, $S=0$ sets? Careful: NAND latch with active-low inputs $\bar{S},\bar{R}$: $\bar{S}=0$ sets $Q=1$, $\bar{R}=0$ resets. Gated SR adds an enable (or clock level): inputs pass only when $EN=1$.

The D latch removes the forbidden state: $D$ goes straight to $S$, inverted to $R$. $EN=1$: transparent ($Q$ follows $D$). $EN=0$: holds. Problem: transparency passes glitches while enabled - which is why edge-triggered flip-flops (next section) run synchronous systems, not latches.

subsections.title: Level-sensitive vs edge-triggered
content: Latch: level-sensitive, transparent during active level. Flip-flop: edge-triggered, samples only at clock rise (or fall).
Synchronous design uses flip-flops so the whole chip updates on one clock edge - timing analysable. Latches appear in special cases (time-borrowing, synchronizers need care).
VEDA waveform questions use D flip-flops (edge), not latches - watch which symbol the question shows.

example.prompt: NOR SR latch with S=1,R=0. State?

subsections.title: Forbidden and race
content: NOR latch $S=R=1$: both NOR outputs $0$, so $Q=\bar{Q}=0$ (not complements). Releasing both to $0$ together: gates race - final state unpredictable (metastability seed).
Design rule: never assert $S$ and $R$ together. D latch enforces this by construction.

subsections.title: Propagation delay first look
content: Every gate/latch takes $t_{pd}$ to react. Outputs change AFTER inputs, never instantly. Waveform sketches must shift edges right by delay.
This delay thinking is the whole of timing analysis (later section).

quickRevision: NOR SR: S sets, R resets, 00 holds, 11 forbidden.
D latch: transparent when EN=1, holds when 0.
readingSections.companyNote: Latch forbidden-state and transparency questions are prelims favourites.

readingSections.title: 2. Flip-Flops - SR, JK, D, T with Tables and Equations
readingSections.quickSummary: Flip-flops sample on the clock edge. D stores, T toggles, JK does everything, SR is the ancestor.
content: Edge triggering (master-slave or edge-detect pulse) makes the device copy input only at the clock edge and ignore it otherwise. Rising-edge is default; a bubble means falling-edge.
D flip-flop: $Q^{+} = D$. The workhorse: registers, counters, FSM state. Asynchronous preset ($PRE=0$ forces $Q=1$) and clear ($CLR=0$ forces $Q=0$) override clock for power-on reset.

JK flip-flop: $Q^{+} = J\bar{Q} + \bar{K}Q$. $J=K=0$ hold, $J=1,K=0$ set, $J=0,K=1$ reset, $J=K=1$ toggle. Fixes SR's forbidden state by toggling instead. Old race-around (level JK oscillating while clock high) is cured by master-slave/edge triggering.
T flip-flop: $Q^{+} = T \oplus Q$. $T=1$ toggles (frequency divide by $2$ per stage - the counter bit), $T=0$ holds. SR flip-flop: clocked SR, $Q^{+} = S + \bar{R}Q$ with $SR=0$.

subsections.title: Reading a flip-flop waveform
content: Mark every active clock edge. At each edge, read $D$ (for D FF) just before the edge (setup) - that becomes $Q$ after clock-to-$Q$ delay.
Between edges $Q$ is frozen regardless of $D$ dancing. Asynchronous clear/preset acts immediately, even between edges.
VEDA Q4 reverses this: from $Q$ waveform deduce the $D$ logic driven by present state.

example.prompt: Rising D FF, D=1 just before edge 1, D=0 before edge 2. Q?
example.answer: Q goes 1 then 0, one edge delayed

subsections.title: Toggle chains divide frequency
content: T=1 (or JK=11) stage toggles each clock: output frequency halves. Two stages divide by $4$, $n$ stages by $2^{n}$ - the binary counter.
Clock dividers in chips are toggle chains with gating for odd ratios.

subsections.title: Preset/clear priority
content: Async $PRE/CLR$ beat clock and usually beat each other by convention ($CLR$ wins if both). In waveforms, a $CLR$ pulse forces $Q=0$ at once.
Power-on reset trees use them; normal operation keeps both inactive.

quickRevision: D: Q+=D. T: Q+=T xor Q. JK: Q+=JQ'+K'Q.
D excitation is trivial: D = next state.
readingSections.companyNote: Excitation tables plus D-waveform reading cover most flip-flop marks.

readingSections.title: 3. Registers and Counters - MOD, Ripple, Ring, Johnson
readingSections.quickSummary: n flip-flops hold n bits and count at most 2^n states. Ripple is simple but slow; synchronous is fast; ring/Johnson trade codes for decoding ease.
content: Registers: PIPO (parallel hold, one clock), SISO (serial delay line, $n$ clocks latency), SIPO/PISO (serial-parallel conversion for UART/SPI). Shift direction (left/right) and rotate variants matter for sequence questions.

Binary counters: $n$ flip-flops give at most $2^{n}$ states, MOD-$M$ uses $M$ of them. Full-sequence MOD-$2^{n}$ needs no reset logic. Truncated MOD-$M$ ($M < 2^{n}$) decodes state $M$ to synchronously/asynchronously reset (e.g. MOD-10 decade: $4$ FFs, clear when $Q_{3}Q_{2}Q_{1}Q_{0} = 1010$, i.e. $CLR = \overline{Q_{3}Q_{1}}$).

Ripple (asynchronous): each stage clocked by previous $Q$ (T=1 everywhere). Simple, but delay adds ($n \times t_{pd}$), max frequency falls, and transient wrong codes appear (glitchy decoding). Synchronous: common clock, T/JK logic per stage ($T_{0}=1, T_{1}=Q_{0}, T_{2}=Q_{1}Q_{0}$...), one $t_{pd}$ per step, clean at speed.

Ring: one $1$ circulates in $n$ FFs (D chain, last $Q$ to first $D$ with single-1 init): $n$ states, one-hot, decodes with NO gates (state = which $Q$ is $1$). Needs start-up/reset into one-hot (forbidden states lock). Johnson (twisted ring): last $\bar{Q}$ fed back: $2n$ states, decodes each state with one $2$-input AND, self-corrects better. Up/down: control $M$ picks $Q$ or $\bar{Q}$ as next clock/data path.

subsections.title: MOD arithmetic in one minute
content: MOD-$M$ counter visits $M$ states then repeats. Binary $n$ FFs: $M \le 2^{n}$, minimum $n = \lceil \log_{2} M \rceil$.
Frequency at last stage of ripple MOD-$M$: $f_{in}/M$ (any counter divides by its MOD).

example.prompt: FFs needed for MOD-10? Reset code?

subsections.title: Ring vs Johnson at a glance
content: Ring $n$ FFs: $n$ states ($1000,0100,0010,0001$ for $n=4$), one-hot, zero decode gates, needs one-hot init.
Johnson $n$ FFs: $2n$ states ($0000,1000,1100,1110,1111,0111,0011,0001$ for $n=4$), $2$-input AND decode, all-zero init works.
Both are shift-register counters, not binary - state order is shift order.

subsections.title: Up/down control idea
content: Binary up uses $Q$ chain ($T_{1}=Q_{0}$); down uses $\bar{Q}$ chain. A $MUX$ per stage with $M$ selects up/down - one extra MUX delay.
In ripple down-counters the previous $\bar{Q}$ clocks the next stage.

quickRevision: MOD-M needs ceil(log2 M) FFs; truncates reset at M.
Ripple O(n) delay, glitchy; synchronous one delay, clean.
Ring n states one-hot; Johnson 2n states, 2-input decode.
readingSections.companyNote: MOD/reset-code and ring-vs-Johnson counts are guaranteed prelims marks.

readingSections.title: 4. Timing - Setup, Hold, Clock-to-Q and Waveform Design (VEDA Q4)
readingSections.quickSummary: Data must be stable around the clock edge (setup before, hold after). VEDA Q4 inverts waveform reading: from Q sequence, find D logic.
content: Setup $t_{su}$: $D$ stable BEFORE edge. Hold $t_{h}$: stable AFTER edge. Clock-to-$Q$ $t_{cq}$: edge to new $Q$. Violate setup/hold and the flop may go metastable (hovers then resolves randomly) - synchronizer chains (2 FFs) absorb input-domain crossings.

Single-flop-plus-comb-loop rule: $T_{clk} \ge t_{cq} + t_{comb} + t_{su}$ (minus helpful skew). So $f_{max} = 1/T_{min}$. Ripple $n$-bit counter needs $T \ge n \times t_{ff}$ roughly; synchronous needs one $t_{cq}+t_{AND}+t_{su}$.

Reading (VEDA Q4 forward): list clock edges, note $D$ before each, draw $Q$ one step delayed. Design (VEDA Q4 asked): given $Q$ waveform and clock, recover required $D$ sequence ($D$ before edge $k$ = $Q$ after edge $k$), write present-state/next-state table over observed states, then $D = Q^{+}$ gives truth table of $D$ in terms of current $Q$s (and inputs), minimise with K-map, draw gates + D FFs.

Sketch discipline: vertical dashed lines at edges, shade setup/hold windows, shift $Q$ by $t_{cq}$, never change $Q$ mid-cycle. Mark async clear pulses separately - they override everything instantly.

subsections.title: VEDA Q4 method step by step
content: Step 1: number the clock edges, sample the given $Q$ waveform into a $Q^{+}$ sequence.
Step 2: shift back one edge: $D_{k} = Q^{+}_{k}$ (D before edge k).
Step 3: tabulate present $Q$ vs required $D$; express $D$ as function of present state bits (K-map).
Step 4: draw minimised gates feeding D, FFs clocked together. Verify by re-simulating two cycles.

example.prompt: Single D FF, Q waveform 0,1,1,0 after edges 1-4. D logic in terms of Q?
steps: D before edge1 = 0 (Q was 0, stays? Q after edge1 = 0? given after-edge sequence 0,1,1,0: D1=0, D2=1, D3=1, D4=0).
Table (Q,D): (0,0),(0,1),(1,1),(1,0): D = not-Q? (0->0? no: (0,0) and (0,1) conflict - needs more state bits or input; single FF insufficient - add a second FF).
Lesson: conflicts reveal needed state width.
example.answer: Method exposes required state - add FFs on conflict

subsections.title: Skew and metastability in one paragraph each
content: Skew: clock arrives at different FFs at different times. Helps hold, hurts setup (or reverse) - budget it in $T_{min}$.
Metastability: sampling changing data can trap a flop mid-rail; resolves in unbounded time. Two-flop synchronizers + MTBF reasoning for clock-domain crossing (CDC).

subsections.title: Async inputs on waveforms
content: Clear/preset pulses act at once, not on edges. After release near an edge, setup/hold (recovery/removal) applies again.
In sketches, draw async-forced segments first, then edge-sampled segments.

quickRevision: Setup before, hold after, cq after edge.
T >= tcq + tcomb + tsu. Ripple T >= n*tff.
readingSections.companyNote: VEDA Q4 is waveform-to-circuit with D FFs - practice the inversion until mechanical.

readingSections.title: 5. FSMs - Mealy vs Moore, Diagrams, Tables, 1011 Detector (VEDA Q5)
readingSections.quickSummary: Moore output depends on state only (clean, one more delay). Mealy depends on state+input (fewer states, faster, can glitch). 1011 non-overlapping Moore needs 5 states.
content: A synchronous FSM = state register (D FFs) + next-state combinational + output combinational. Moore: $Z = f(state)$ written inside the state circle; output changes only on clock edges (clean). Mealy: $Z = f(state,input)$ written on transitions as input/output; reacts immediately (fewer states, possible input-glitch feedthrough).

State diagram: circles = states (Moore: name/output inside), arcs = transitions labelled input (Mealy: input/output). State table: present-state + input columns, next-state + output columns - the synthesis-ready form. Equivalent states (same next/outputs for all inputs) merge to minimise.

VEDA Q5: synchronous Moore FSM detecting non-overlapping $1011$. Five states: $S_{0}$ idle, $S_{1}$ got $1$, $S_{2}$ got $10$, $S_{3}$ got $101$, $S_{4}$ got $1011$ with output $1$ (others $0$). Transitions: $S_{0}$: $0\to S_{0}$, $1\to S_{1}$. $S_{1}$: $0\to S_{2}$, $1\to S_{1}$. $S_{2}$: $0\to S_{0}$, $1\to S_{3}$. $S_{3}$: $0\to S_{2}$, $1\to S_{4}$. $S_{4}$ (non-overlapping restart): $0\to S_{0}$, $1\to S_{1}$. Output: $Z=1$ only in $S_{4}$.

Overlapping vs non-overlapping: overlapping reuses the tail (for $1011$, from $S_{4}$: $0\to S_{2}$ since $10$ is a prefix, $1\to S_{1}$). Non-overlapping restarts ($S_{4}$: $0\to S_{0}$, $1\to S_{1}$) - which VEDA asks. Sequence check $1101011$: non-overlapping detects once at the end; overlapping would also catch earlier embedded copies.

subsections.title: Mealy 1011 for contrast (3-4 states)
content: Mealy can output during the transition into the last bit, saving the terminal state: typically $4$ states ($S_{0},S_{1},S_{2},S_{3}$) with the $S_{3},1/1$ arc asserting $Z$.
Cost: output timing depends on input arrival within the cycle - glitch-prone, harder timing closure. Mains answers should state the trade-off when choosing.

example.prompt: States for non-overlapping 1011: Moore vs Mealy?
steps: Moore needs distinct output state: $5$ states.
Same detection, one cycle earlier visibility in Mealy.

subsections.title: Drawing discipline that earns marks
content: Moore: output inside every circle. Mealy: every arc labelled in/out. Reset arc to $S_{0}$ drawn. Self-loops explicit ($S_{1},1\to S_{1}$).
Synchronous: note single clock for all FFs; outputs registered (Moore) or combinational (Mealy).

subsections.title: State minimisation glance
content: Row matching (same next-states and outputs for all inputs) merges compatible states; implication charts systematise it.
Binary assign $\lceil \log_{2} S \rceil$ FFs ($5$ states need $3$ FFs); one-hot ($5$ FFs) simplifies decode at area cost - FPGAs love one-hot.

quickRevision: Moore Z=f(state): clean, +1 state. Mealy Z=f(state,input): compact, glitchy.
1011 non-overlap Moore: S0..S4, Z=1 only in S4.
Tables are diagrams in synthesizable form.
readingSections.companyNote: VEDA Q5 is the diagram question - draw the 5-state Moore with outputs in circles.

readingSections.title: 6. Synchronous Design Procedure - States to Gates
readingSections.quickSummary: Spec, diagram, table, codes, excitation, K-maps, circuit. With D flip-flops the K-map inputs are just next-state bits.
content: Procedure: (1) word spec + Moore/Mealy choice, (2) state diagram, (3) state table (present, input, next, output), (4) state assignment (binary needs $\lceil \log_{2} S \rceil$ FFs), (5) transition table with FF excitation ($D = Q^{+}$ for D FFs - no separate excitation table needed), (6) K-map each $D$ and each output, (7) draw FFs + minimised gates + single clock + async reset, (8) verify by cycle simulation including reset and one full pattern.

Timing closure note (syllabus: for functionality AND timing): compute $T_{min} = t_{cq} + t_{comb} + t_{su}$ on the longest $Q$-to-$D$ path; if violated, pipeline, use faster library cells, or one-hot encode to cut decode depth. Mention this line in mains design answers.
Unused states ($5$-state machine in $3$ FFs has $3$ unused): route them to reset (safe FSM) or mark don't-care for area - state your choice; safe recovery beats minimal gates in silicon.

subsections.title: Why D flip-flops dominate exams and chips
content: Excitation $D = Q^{+}$ skips tables - fewer mistakes under time pressure.
Standard-cell and FPGA flows map D FFs + LUT/comb directly; JK/T are teaching tools and special dividers.
VEDA Q4/Q5 both say D flip-flops - obey the question.

subsections.title: Verification checklist
content: Reset reaches $S_{0}$. One legal pattern walk matches spec. One illegal/overlap input behaves as specified. No unintended latch (all $D$s fully specified).
State your clocking (single rising edge) and reset (async active-low typical).

subsections.title: Area vs speed remarks
content: Binary coding: fewer FFs, deeper decode. One-hot: more FFs, shallow fast decode, easy illegal-state detect.
Shares product terms across $D$s and outputs where K-maps align.

quickRevision: Diagram, table, codes, D=Q+ maps, gates, verify.
readingSections.companyNote: A complete small design (counter or 101 detector next-state) with timing line is a full-marks mains answer.

formulas.title: Flip-Flops Needed and MOD

formula.text: n flip-flops hold at most 2^n states. MOD-M visits M states; truncated counters reset at state M.

explanation: Full binary MOD-2^n uses all states.
Truncated MOD-M decodes state M to clear.
Last-stage frequency is fin divided by M.
formulas.commonMistake: Using 3 FFs for MOD-5+ (only 8 states max is fine for 5 - wait 3 FFs give 8 states so MOD-5 OK; MOD-10 needs 4).

formulas.title: D Characteristic and Excitation

formula.text: Next state equals D. Required D equals desired next state - trivial excitation.

formulas.whenToUse: All D flip-flop analysis and design.
explanation: Sample D at edge, Q follows after tcq.
Design: write next-state column, that IS the D map.
formulas.memoryTip: D stands for Data and for Direct.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding excitation tables for D - unnecessary.

formulas.title: JK Characteristic

formula.text: Hold, set, reset, toggle by J,K. J=K=1 toggles.

explanation: 00 hold, 10 set, 01 reset, 11 toggle.
formulas.memoryTip: JK = fancy SR with toggle instead of forbidden.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting K bar in second term.

formulas.title: T Characteristic

formula.latex: Q^{+} = T \oplus Q, \quad T_{req} = Q \oplus Q^{+}
formula.text: T=1 toggles, T=0 holds. Each toggle stage halves frequency.

explanation: Ripple counter ties all T=1.
Sync counter computes T per stage.
formulas.commonMistake: T=0 does not reset - it holds.

formulas.title: SR (Clocked) Characteristic

formula.text: Set dominates with reset held off. SR=1 forbidden.

explanation: Excitation mirrors latch set/reset/hold.
Never assert both.
formulas.memoryTip: S sets, R resets, both banished.

formulas.title: Clock Period Rule

formula.text: Worst Q-to-D path must fit: flop delay plus logic plus setup. Skew subtracts margin.

explanation: Ripple n-bit needs about n flop delays.
Sync needs one cq plus decode plus setup.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting hold is a separate min-delay check, not period.

formulas.title: Ring and Johnson Counts

formula.text: Ring circulates one 1. Johnson circulates with inversion, doubling states.

explanation: Ring one-hot: state = position of 1.
formulas.commonMistake: Calling Johnson 2^n - it is linear, not exponential.

formulas.title: Moore vs Mealy Outputs

formula.text: Moore changes on edges only. Mealy reacts within the cycle and usually needs fewer states.

explanation: 1011 non-overlap: Moore 5 states, Mealy 4.
Mealy outputs can glitch with input.

example.prompt: Output 1 only inside a state. Type?

formulas.title: Truncated-Counter Reset Decode

formula.text: NAND the 1-bits of M's code to clear. Use minimal product (e.g. Q3Q1 for 1010).

explanation: MOD-10: clear at 1010 via Q3Q1.
MOD-5: clear at 101.
formulas.memoryTip: Reset at the first UNUSED code.
formulas.commonMistake: Decoding M-1 (last used) instead of M.

formulas.title: Waveform Inversion (Q to D)

formula.latex: D_{k} = Q^{+}_{k} \text{ (D before edge k = Q after edge k)}
formula.text: Design from waveform runs reading backwards: required D is the observed next Q.

explanation: Sample Q after each edge.
Shift back one edge to get D.
Map D against present state, minimise.

example.prompt: Q after edges: 0,1,1. D before edges?

formulas.memoryTip: D leads, Q lags by one edge.
formulas.commonMistake: Aligning D and Q to the same edge.

exp: Latch obeys levels; flop samples edges.
D stores: next equals data at edge.
Setup guards sampling: $D$ ready before edge.
Hold keeps $D$ past the edge so sampling completes.
Bit shifts one stage per clock.

Stay $1$: do not reset, set don't-care.

First may go metastable; second samples settled value.
Late clock steals setup time downstream.

Output on $S_{3},1$ arc: no terminal state.
Bits 1-4 walk S0-1S1-0S2-1S3-1S4: detect 1 at bit 4.
$J=K=1$ toggles repeatedly during long high clock.
Master loads, slave copies on opposite phase.
